input_template: Configure a transient prediction case for ieee14_load_step: IEEE 14-bus sudden load increase (no fault); observes frequency response and rotor angle deviation; fault_duration=0. Use the following parameterization: V_base_kv = {value_0} kV for base voltage of the bus system; load scaling factor relative to base case (load_scale) takes {value_1}; P_load_mean (mean active power load per bus) is {value_2} MW; P_load_std, representing standard deviation of active power load, is set to {value_3} MW; Q_load_ratio = {value_4} for ratio of reactive to active load. Additional controls are total active power generation before disturbance (P_gen_total) takes {value_5} MW; renewable_ratio (fraction of generation from renewables (affects inertia)) is {value_6}; fault_duration, representing fault clearing time (0 for load-step scenarios, 0.05-0.25s for fault scenarios), is set to {value_7} s; grid_voltage_pu = {value_8} pu for pre-disturbance bus voltage setpoint; number of buses (14 for all IEEE14 scenarios) (n_buses) takes {value_9}. Remaining physical or categorical settings are inertia_mean (mean generator inertia constant H (scales all generators)) is {value_10} s; damping_mean, representing mean generator damping coefficient D, is set to {value_11}; line_loading = {value_12} for pre-disturbance line loading factor; pre-disturbance voltage deviation (voltage_dev) takes {value_13} pu after being at 1/8 of nominal; freq_dev (pre-disturbance frequency deviation) is {value_14} Hz. Use full 10-second trajectory, 1000 time steps at 100 Hz; observed channels: generator 1, generator 2, generator 3, generator 4, generator 5 (5 of 5) and predict rotor_angles.
target_template: Model output for rotor_angles:{output_0}
